Packets are printed on **A3 and folded** into a booklet of A4 pages. These samples show every page layout Chalkline has for them, in three print themes. Pick the closest page, then copy its piece (the names in *Made of* below) from `_extensions/chalkline/typst/packet/`. The kit's README explains each piece.

## Write packet pages in .qmd

Every printable's PDF now uses the kit: the theme comes from `packet-theme: sky` (or `trail`, `blueprint`) in its labels, and the teacher site prints the teacher edition, with the answers written in. Write the pieces as blocks. In a list, `|` separates the parts, and **answers print only in the teacher edition**. See **Roads and Water** (`guide/samples/roads-practice.qmd`) for a page written this way.

| Block | Write | In the PDF |
|---|---|---|
| `::: vocab-hunt` | `- ¶2 \| _n._ small stones \| gravel` (where · clue · word) | Where / Clue / Word, in two tables |
| `::: recall` | `- Why did Rome need roads? \| To move soldiers.` | two answer lines each |
| `::: {.sequence order="3,1,2"}` | one event per line | boxes for the order |
| `::: {.problems cols="2"}` | `- $3x + 5 = 20$ \| 5 \| 3x = 15` (problem · answer · working) | tall boxes with a grid, an answer box |
| `::: {.work-space height="4cm" style="lines" label="…"}` | `height="fill"`: the rest of the page; `style`: blank, lines, grid, dots | a box to write or draw in |
| `::: side-by-side` | two or three blocks inside; `widths="3, 2"` for unequal widths | half-width (or third) spaces |
| `::: {.picture-steps height="31mm"}` | `- ![](images/a.jpg) \| Title \| What happens.` (one step per line) | pictures down the left third, each step's number, title and words beside it |
| `::: {.picture-column title="…" height="46mm"}` | the pictures (`![Caption](images/a.jpg)`), then the text | pictures down the left third, the text in one box beside them |
| a Markdown table | `\| Part \| What it does \|` | the page's width, the theme's colours; `: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}` sets the widths |
| `::: {.kwl title="…" topic="…"}` |  | a landscape KWL |
| `::: {.venn title="…" a="…" b="…"}` | the "So what?" question inside | the landscape Venn |
| `::: {.frayer id="ROM-011"}` |  | a Frayer model from the vocab list |
| `::: {.cause-effect event="…"}`, `::: flow`, `::: {.web topic="…" branches="a, b, c"}`, `::: temple` | the "So what?" question inside | the other organizers |
| `::: {.investigation letter="A" sources="…, …"}` |  | Observe, Infer, Evidence |
| `::: {.self-check lesson="true"}` | `- name five kinds of angle.` (one "I can" per line) | four stars to colour each; without `lesson`, 1 2 3 at the start and the end of the unit |
| `::: {.source-card number="1" title="…" size="1215x2000" crop="…" markers="1: 760,175"}` | the picture (`![](images/x.jpg)`), the caption, then `::: glance`, `::: look-closely`, `::: source-context`, `::: source-quote`, `::: source-cite` | a whole-page primary source card (see the Mesopotamia example) |
| `::: {.test-head title="…" unit="…" total="25"}` | the instructions inside | a test's heading: marks box, Name, instructions |
| `::: short-answer` | `- [2] Question? \| 中文 \| answer` (`[2/1]`: 2 marks, 1 line) | numbered questions with marks and lines |
| `::: {.rubric term="explain" criterion="…"}` | `- 5–6 \| what it looks like \| an example \| target` | the rubric table, the target level marked |
| `::: {.command-term term="explain" zh="解释"}` | what it means inside | the command term, big |
| `::: paragraph-chain` | `- The challenge \| a hint` | linked boxes to plan a paragraph |
| `::: {.writing-lines lines="13"}` |  | lines, with a circle to tick each sentence |
| `::: design-artifact`, `::: {.subunit number="1.2" title="…"}` |  | the design challenge page; a line in the packet's contents |
| `::: {.page-about name="…" uses="…; …" pieces="…"}` |  | a hidden note: what the page is for |

On the web, each page shows its words (questions, problems, events) without the answers; diagrams say to use the PDF.

**Unit packets are booklets now.** `python chalkline.py packets` (and every full render) builds each unit's packet with the kit:
- a title page (the unit's number and name, the course, the school);
- the contents (from each printable's title) and the unit's "I can" objectives;
- each printable starting on a new page;
- Notes pages and a back cover, so the page count is a multiple of 4.

The theme comes from `packet-theme:` in `_quarto.yml`. Put an empty `::: spread` block at the top of a printable to start it on a left-hand page, facing the next one.

Each printable's own PDF (a loose sheet) says where it is in the packet, "Goes with packet page 5", at the foot of the page. The page comes from the last packet build (`generated/packet-pages.json`), so a new printable gets its label from the next full build.

**The cover.** The title page shows the school's logo (from `brand/`), the unit's title, and the teacher's name from `teacher:` in `course/season.yml`. For a cover picture, add two labels to the unit's `index.qmd`:

```yaml
packet-hero: images/colosseum-forum.jpg      # a wide photo from the unit's folder
packet-hero-credit: "the Colosseum and the Roman Forum, by Wilfredor, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons"
```

The credit is printed on the back cover, under **Picture credits**.

## How a packet works

- **One design, two ways to print.** The whole packet is an A3 booklet: facing pages, and Notes pages added at the end so the page count is a multiple of 4. Any single worksheet can also be printed on its own (a *loose sheet*): A4, with a name line, "Page 1 of 2" and "Goes with packet page 15". A two-page spread prints as two pages; a Venn or KWL as a landscape page.
- **Spreads.** A page can start a spread: it always lands on a left-hand page. If that would leave an empty page, it becomes a Notes page.
- **The teacher edition** is the same packet with the answers written in, in red handwriting, where students write theirs. Nothing moves, so the teacher's page 11 is the student's page 11.
- **Themes for paper.** Sky, Trail and Blueprint (Night, for paper) put colour only in lines and small marks, so they still look right on the school's black-and-white copier. Print the **printer check** once, photocopy it, and see what survives.
- **Words and language come from the lists.** Key word cards, Frayer models, glosses and language pages read `vocab/data/vocab.csv` and `frames.csv`, so they always match the vocab list.

## Every page, and what it's for

The notes come from each page itself: every page in the samples carries a hidden note with its name, its uses and its pieces. They aren't printed; the build reads them.

<div id="packet-catalog"><p><em>The list of pages appears here after a full render of the teacher site.</em></p></div>

```{=html}
<style>
#packet-catalog table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.92rem; }
#packet-catalog th, #packet-catalog td { text-align: left; vertical-align: top; padding: 0.4rem 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #e3e8ef; }
#packet-catalog th { font-size: 0.8rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #52606d; }
#packet-catalog .pk-name { font-weight: 700; color: #003477; white-space: nowrap; }
#packet-catalog .pk-uses { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.1rem; }
#packet-catalog code { font-size: 0.8rem; }
#packet-catalog .pk-sample { color: #52606d; font-size: 0.82rem; }
</style>
<script>
fetch("packet/packet-templates.json").then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : null).then(rows => {
  if (!rows || !rows.length) return;
  const name = {};
  const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" }[c]));
  let html = "<table><thead><tr><th>Page</th><th>Use it for</th><th>Made of</th></tr></thead><tbody>";
  for (const r of rows) {
    html += "<tr><td><span class='pk-name'>" + esc(r.name) + "</span><br><a class='pk-sample' href='" + esc(r.pdf) + "#page=" + r.page + "' target='_blank'>" +
      esc(r.sample || name[r.pdf] || r.pdf) + ", page " + r.page + "</a></td><td><ul class='pk-uses'>" +
      (r.uses || []).map(u => "<li>" + esc(u) + "</li>").join("") + "</ul></td><td>" +
      (r.pieces || []).map(p => "<code>" + esc(p) + "</code>").join(" ") + "</td></tr>";
  }
  document.getElementById("packet-catalog").innerHTML = html + "</tbody></table>";
}).catch(() => {});
</script>
```

## The Rome example (40 pages, written in .qmd)

The Ancient Rome example unit's packet uses every kind of page: title page and contents, a magazine feature spread, a glossed reading spread, key words and the language page, a vocabulary hunt, a KWL, a reading with a questions box, a landscape chart, math in two and three columns, a reference and design spread, a timeline across a spread, the graphic organizers, the page layouts with pictures (a mixed page with tables, picture steps, a picture column) and a self-check. Every page is a `.qmd` file in [Ancient Rome](examples/example-rome/index.qmd).

{{< pdf-viewer "examples/example-rome/example-rome-packet.pdf" layout="gallery" title="Rome example · Sky" >}}

**The same packet, other themes:** [Trail](examples/example-rome/example-rome-packet-trail.pdf) · [Blueprint](examples/example-rome/example-rome-packet-blueprint.pdf) · [Teacher edition (Sky)](examples/example-rome/example-rome-teacher-packet.pdf). A unit asks for these with `packet-themes: [trail, blueprint]` in its `index.qmd`.

## The Mesopotamia example (12 pages, written in .qmd)

Rebuilt from a teacher's own worksheets, as an example unit you can copy: a source dossier spread (real museum photos with numbered markers), two source investigations, a design-your-own-artifact challenge, and a formative assessment with marks, a rubric and a paragraph planner. Every page is a `.qmd` file written with the history blocks below; see [Mesopotamia](examples/example-mesopotamia/index.qmd).

{{< pdf-viewer "examples/example-mesopotamia/example-mesopotamia-packet.pdf" layout="gallery" title="Mesopotamia example · Trail" >}}

**Teacher edition:** [the same packet with the answers written in](examples/example-mesopotamia/example-mesopotamia-teacher-packet.pdf)

## Loose sheets and the printer check

Every page of the example units is also a loose sheet: open a page in [Ancient Rome](examples/example-rome/index.qmd) and use its PDF (A4, with Name, "Page 1 of 2" and "Goes with packet page …"). Print the [**printer check**](packet/printer-test.pdf) once (one page per theme: print it, photocopy the print, tick what still shows).
